steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Voting in elections is the most basic form of democratic participation, but citizens have many other routes to influence decisions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Petitions to Parliament: if a petition on the UK Parliament website reaches 100,000 signatures, it must be considered for debate in Parliament. Petitions are a direct way for citizens to raise issues.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Pressure groups are organisations that aim to influence government policy without seeking election. Insider groups (e.g. BMA, CBI) have regular access to government. Outsider groups (e.g. Greenpeace, Extinction Rebellion) use public campaigns and direct action.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Lobbying involves directly contacting MPs, peers, or ministers to influence legislation or policy. Professional lobbying is a major industry, raising concerns about unequal access for wealthy interests.
